speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance in respect of the payment of $300 to Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) Plus holders who are spouses of Singaporeans, whether such a payment may also be extended to LTVP holders who are spouses of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are also many Social Service Agencies and those in the community providing support to families in need.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: My query is in relation to the policy reason for carving out LTVP holders from the LTVP+ holders who would be able to get Solidarity payments, given as I understand the rationale behind the issuing of Solidarity payments to Singapore PRs and the LTVP+ holders is really to help the family.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: LTVP holders who are spouses are also part of the families as well.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For LTVP and LTVP+, we have in our system different sets of support for various schemes for different groups of people, one of them being their residential status.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, we need some clear alignment of this.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Therefore, this is a way that we are aligning this, with existing schemes that we have.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Bear in mind that this support is for a very urgent situation and therefore, we have extended it to a wide range.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There are already many support schemes, as I have said.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The assurance that I would like to give Mr Murali is that, as I have said, if families need support, they can approach our Social Service Agencies and many other service agencies that are providing this support.
